about.text: Soft cheese ripened under a white rind of mould, Penicillium camemberti, whose enzymes break down its protein from the surface towards the centre, so that it softens from the outside in. Brie and Camembert are the classic examples.

picks.why: The archetype of bloomy-rind cheese, born in Normandy around 1791 and imitated in dozens of countries.
The PDO Brie of Seine-et-Marne, long called the king of cheeses and the benchmark for every brie.
A celebrated Normandy triple cream, the defining rich, buttery bloomy cheese of French cheese boards.
A PDO Champagne cheese, among the oldest in France, made since the Middle Ages.
A German blue-and-white-mould hybrid made industrially in huge volumes and sold worldwide.
